f0.text:
name: Companions

# Keeps the companion images core embeds present in the registry. core pins
# each companion tag (codeflydev/<name>:<version>) via info.codefly.yaml and
# agents pull those exact tags at runtime, so a pinned-but-unpushed tag
# breaks every Codefly-native build at the companion pull.
#
# Two jobs:
#   publish - an explicit operator action that builds+pushes the whole set,
#             then verifies it. This requires Docker Hub release credentials.
#   verify  - a standing gate (CLI release + daily) that fails fast when an
#             embedded public tag is missing, without mutating the registry.
#
# The fail-fast-on-bump gate ideally also lives in core's CI (that is where
# companion versions change); this repo runs it against core@main on a
# schedule so a regression surfaces here too.

on:
  release:
    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Daily, so an embedded tag that goes missing is caught within a day.
    - cron: '0 6 * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      core_ref:
        description: 'core ref (tag/branch/sha) to publish/verify companions from'
        required: false
        default: 'main'

# Publishing mutates immutable tags. Two overlapping runs would interleave those
# pushes, leaving each tag naming whichever run finished last while both report
# success. Queue instead of cancelling: a cancelled run would leave the fleet
# half-published.
concurrency:
  group: companions-publish
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  publish:
    name: Publish and verify companion images
    # Companion versions are owned by core, not by the CLI version. Publishing
    # is therefore an explicit registry mutation, never a side effect of every
    # unrelated CLI release.
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # 360 minutes is the GitHub-hosted ceiling, not a tunable: no value here
    # can buy this job more time. It is set explicitly because the whole set is
    # built serially and the proto image compiles ~10 Go plugins with its arm64
    # half under QEMU, so the run is within sight of the cap. If it starts
    # timing out, the fix is to fan the companions out across jobs — the base
    # first, then its dependents, which is now possible because a dependent
    # resolves its base from the registry through CODEFLY_BASE_IMAGE rather
    # than from a locally-built image.
    timeout-minutes: 360
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write
      id-token: write
      attestations: write
    outputs:
      companions: ${{ steps.published.outputs.companions }}
    steps:
      - name: Check out cli
        uses: actions/checkout@fbc6f3992d24b796d5a048ff273f7fcc4a7b6c09 # v5
        with:
          path: cli

      - name: Check out core
        uses: actions/checkout@fbc6f3992d24b796d5a048ff273f7fcc4a7b6c09 # v5
        with:
          repository: codefly-dev/core
          ref: ${{ github.event.inputs.core_ref || 'main' }}
          token: ${{ secrets.GH_PAT }}
          # buildLinuxCLI expects core/ and cli/ as siblings: language
          # companions COPY --from a linux binary cross-compiled from ../cli.
          path: core

      - name: Set up Go
        uses: actions/setup-go@924ae3a1cded613372ab5595356fb5720e22ba16 # v6
        with:
          go-version-file: cli/go.mod
          cache: false

      - name: Build the codefly CLI
        working-directory: cli
        run: GOWORK=off GOBIN="${{ github.workspace }}/bin" go install ./cmd/codefly

      # A multi-platform buildx push builds every image as one manifest, so the
      # arm64 stages need an emulator (QEMU) and a builder that can emit a
      # manifest list.
      - name: Set up QEMU
        uses: docker/setup-qemu-action@c7c53464625b32c7a7e944ae62b3e17d2b600130 # v3

      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@8d2750c68a42422c14e847fe6c8ac0403b4cbd6f # v3

      # Companion tags resolve through resources.ImageRegistry, which is
      # ghcr.io/codefly-dev — authenticating anywhere else leaves every push
      # unauthenticated and the whole run publishes nothing.
      - name: Log in to GitHub Container Registry
        uses: docker/login-action@c94ce9fb468520275223c153574b00df6fe4bcc9 # v3
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Publish every companion at its pinned version
        # Publish multi-arch: every language service agent ships linux/arm64, so
        # a companion must too or it can't run a single language service on an
        # arm64 host. One manifest list serves both arches.
        #
        # --force-docker: proto ships a flake.nix and the nix path cannot emit a
        # multi-platform manifest, so a runner with nix installed would abort
        # the run on proto after the earlier companions were already pushed.
        # --pull: refreshes the floating upstream bases the Dockerfiles sit on
        # (golang:1.27-alpine, node:...-alpine) so a rebuild picks up their
        # latest patch instead of a cached older layer. It has nothing to do
        # with the codefly base companion: that one is resolved by reference
        # and passed as CODEFLY_BASE_IMAGE, not inherited from the cache.
        # --published-manifest: records what this run actually pushed, which is
        # the only set that may be attested below.
        run: >-
          ${{ github.workspace }}/bin/codefly companion publish --all
          --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64
          --force-docker
          --pull
          --core-dir "${{ github.workspace }}/core"
          --published-manifest "${{ runner.temp }}/published.json"

      # Written whether or not publish succeeded, so a partial run still
      # attests the companions it did push. `if: always()` covers the publish
      # step failing; the file is absent only if publish never ran at all.
      - name: Collect what this run published
        id: published
        if: always()
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          file="${{ runner.temp }}/published.json"
          # Absent means publish never reached the build: report an empty set
          # rather than failing here and masking the real failure above. A file
          # that exists but does not parse is a different matter and must fail.
          if [ ! -f "$file" ]; then
            echo "companions=[]" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            exit 0
          fi
          echo "companions=$(jq -c . "$file")" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Verify every embedded tag is in the registry
        run: ${{ github.workspace }}/bin/codefly companion verify --core-dir "${{ github.workspace }}/core"

  # Provenance is attested per image because actions/attest-build-provenance
  # signs one subject at a time.
  #
  # The matrix is what the publish run reported pushing, never the full set
  # core declares. A build-provenance attestation asserts that this workflow
  # run produced these bits, so attesting a tag the run skipped as already
  # published would sign a claim that is simply false — and it is pushed to
  # the registry and a public transparency log, where it cannot be withdrawn.
  attest:
    name: Attest published companion images
    needs: publish
    # An empty matrix produces no jobs, which is the correct outcome when a run
    # published nothing. The guard is for the publish job failing outright.
    if: needs.publish.outputs.companions != '' && needs.publish.outputs.companions != '[]'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      # write, not read: push-to-registry uploads the attestation to ghcr as an
      # OCI artifact, which read cannot do — it 403s after publish has already
      # mutated the registry.
      packages: write
      id-token: write
      attestations: write
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include: ${{ fromJSON(needs.publish.outputs.companions) }}
    steps:
      - uses: docker/login-action@c94ce9fb468520275223c153574b00df6fe4bcc9 # v3
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      # The digest comes from the publish run's own report of what it pushed,
      # not from resolving the tag here. A tag is mutable and this job runs after
      # the whole publish job has finished, so re-reading it could attest an
      # image this workflow run never built — a claim that is then pushed to a
      # public transparency log, where it cannot be withdrawn.
      - name: Check the publish run reported a digest
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -z "${{ matrix.digest }}" ]; then
            echo "publish reported no digest for ${{ matrix.image }}; refusing to attest an image this run cannot name exactly" >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      - uses: actions/attest-build-provenance@e8998f949152b193b063cb0ec769d69d929409be # v2
        with:
          subject-name: ghcr.io/codefly-dev/${{ matrix.companion }}
          subject-digest: ${{ matrix.digest }}
          push-to-registry: true

  verify:
    name: Verify embedded companion tags
    # Standing read-only gate. A manual run uses the publish job above, whose
    # final step verifies the same immutable tags after pushing.
    if: github.event_name == 'release' || github.event_name == 'schedule'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Check out cli
        uses: actions/checkout@fbc6f3992d24b796d5a048ff273f7fcc4a7b6c09 # v5
        with:
          path: cli

      - name: Check out core
        uses: actions/checkout@fbc6f3992d24b796d5a048ff273f7fcc4a7b6c09 # v5
        with:
          repository: codefly-dev/core
          ref: ${{ github.event.inputs.core_ref || 'main' }}
          token: ${{ secrets.GH_PAT }}
          path: core

      - name: Set up Go
        uses: actions/setup-go@924ae3a1cded613372ab5595356fb5720e22ba16 # v6
        with:
          go-version-file: cli/go.mod
          cache: false

      - name: Build the codefly CLI
        working-directory: cli
        run: GOWORK=off GOBIN="${{ github.workspace }}/bin" go install ./cmd/codefly

      - name: Verify a linux/arm64 companion can resolve every language agent
        # Guards the arm64 companion footgun: publishing an arm64 companion is
        # only safe while every language agent still ships a linux/arm64 asset.
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GH_PAT }}
        run: ${{ github.workspace }}/bin/codefly agent verify-platform linux/arm64

      - name: Verify every embedded tag is in the registry
        run: ${{ github.workspace }}/bin/codefly companion verify --core-dir "${{ github.workspace }}/core"

name: Go CLI

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main ]

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  quality:
    name: ${{ matrix.gate }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # The race and coverage gates take 4-5 minutes on a warm cache with ±40s of
    # runner variance, so a 5-minute budget cancels borderline-healthy runs.
    # 8 minutes keeps a hang from burning a full runner-hour while leaving the
    # suite real headroom.
    timeout-minutes: 8
    # `conformance_rows` is the set of docs/supported-matrix.md rows this gate
    # claims to prove. A claimed row's tests can no longer skip themselves when
    # the backend is missing, and the always-run receipt check below fails if a
    # claimed row never ran.
    env:
      CODEFLY_CONFORMANCE_REQUIRED: ${{ matrix.conformance_rows }}
      CODEFLY_CONFORMANCE_RECEIPTS: ${{ github.workspace }}/conformance-receipts
    strategy:
      fail-fast: true
      matrix:
        include:
          - gate: bootstrap-audit
          - gate: control-integration
            conformance_rows: linux-amd64-nix-run
          - gate: coverage
            conformance_rows: linux-amd64-source,linux-amd64-native-npm
          - gate: race
            conformance_rows: linux-amd64-source,linux-amd64-native-npm
    steps:
      - name: checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@fbc6f3992d24b796d5a048ff273f7fcc4a7b6c09 # v5

      - name: Set up Go
        if: matrix.gate == 'coverage' || matrix.gate == 'race'
        uses: actions/setup-go@924ae3a1cded613372ab5595356fb5720e22ba16 # v6
        with:
          go-version-file: go.mod
          cache: false

      # The production source-workspace regression runs the released Python
      # plugin on a fresh Linux host. Provision its declared uv runtime in the
      # ordinary test lanes so the proof exercises real tests instead of an
      # environment-blocked agent response.
      - name: Set up uv
        if: matrix.gate == 'coverage' || matrix.gate == 'race'
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@c771a70e6277c0a99b617c7a806ffedaca235ff9 # v9.0.0

      # pkg/librarystore's npm backend shells out to the real npm CLI (npm pack,
      # npm publish) against an httptest registry rather than mocking the store;
      # those tests need node/npm on the runner.
      - name: Set up Node
        if: matrix.gate == 'coverage' || matrix.gate == 'race'
        uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7

      # Restore before the bootstrap action: that action compiles the CLI, so
      # restoring afterward would make its cache permanently ineffective.
      # Cache only compiled artifacts. Caching GOMODCACHE alongside a Go
      # toolchain directive can race setup-go's toolchain install and produce
      # tar restore conflicts.
      - name: Restore Go build cache
        uses: actions/cache@caa296126883cff596d87d8935842f9db880ef25 # v5
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/go-build
          key: cli-go-build-v3-${{ matrix.gate }}-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('go.sum') }}
          restore-keys: |
            cli-go-build-v3-${{ matrix.gate }}-${{ runner.os }}-

      # This is both the canonical bootstrap and the cross-repository action
      # contract consumed by Codefly products. Dogfood the local action so a
      # release cannot publish an installer that CI never exercised.
      - name: install Codefly
        if: matrix.gate == 'bootstrap-audit' || matrix.gate == 'control-integration'
        uses: ./.github/actions/install

      - name: Install Dependencies
        run: go mod download

      - name: Verify the composed-module command is packaged
        if: matrix.gate == 'bootstrap-audit'
        run: codefly sync module --help

      # govulncheck gate via the CLI (replaces scripts/govulncheck.sh):
      # suppressions + staleness from .govulncheck.yaml, fails only on
      # actionable (upstream-fixed) findings.
      - name: govulncheck audit
        if: matrix.gate == 'bootstrap-audit'
        run: |
          go install golang.org/x/vuln/cmd/govulncheck@latest
          codefly audit go --dir .

      - name: Test with coverage
        if: matrix.gate == 'coverage'
        run: go test -failfast ./... -coverprofile=cover.out -covermode=atomic -coverpkg=./...

      - name: Check test coverage
        if: matrix.gate == 'coverage'
        id: coverage
        uses: vladopajic/go-test-coverage@f94bcf0d6b9fa5fb8b783830b22648f6c17475e2 # v2
        with:
          config: ./.testcoverage.yaml

      # The CGO-free companion/self-cross build (`-tags codefly_nosemantic`,
      # CGO_ENABLED=0) selects pkg/engine/source_nosemantic.go. `codefly
      # companion publish` exercises it only in companions.yaml, which needs
      # Docker; verify here, unconditionally, that the variant both links
      # statically and runs its base source behavior. Without this a regression
      # in the analyzer-free variant would surface only at publish time.
      - name: Verify CGO-free (companion) build variant
        if: matrix.gate == 'coverage'
        env:
          CGO_ENABLED: "0"
        run: |
          go build -tags codefly_nosemantic -ldflags '-s -w -extldflags "-static"' -o /dev/null .
          go test -tags codefly_nosemantic ./pkg/engine/ -run '^TestNewSourceExecutesLanguageNeutralOperation$' -count=1

      - name: Test with race detection
        if: matrix.gate == 'race'
        run: go test -failfast -race ./... -v

      # The cross-process control-ownership proof drives the CLI built by the
      # install action above as a real subprocess against real sockets. It runs
      # here rather than in the default lanes because those would have to link
      # a CLI binary of their own; it needs neither Nix nor an agent, so it runs
      # before both and fails fast.
      - name: Run the cross-process control-ownership proof
        if: matrix.gate == 'control-integration'
        run: go test -tags=integration -run '^TestRunRefusesAControlAddressAnotherProcessOwns$|^TestConcurrentDisposableRunsClaimDistinctIdentities$' ./cmd/run -v

      # The pinned Redis agent resolves a Nix runtime during runtime-init, so the
      # proof needs Nix on the runner or the agent fails with "nix is not
      # installed" instead of exercising the real dependency. Mirrors core's CI.
      - name: Install Nix
        # Strict — nix is core to the platform; if it doesn't install,
        # CI must fail loud rather than silently skipping nix tests.
        # DeterminateSystems' installer is the de-facto standard for
        # GH Actions: deterministic, no daemon issues on ephemeral runners.
        #
        # This used to follow @main. It is now pinned to a release, like every
        # other action here, so the comment records the tag at the pinned commit
        # (v23) rather than the branch it was reached through — Dependabot
        # resolves the version from the tag at the SHA, so a `# main` comment
        # would be silently rewritten to a version on the first bump.
        if: matrix.gate == 'control-integration'
        uses: DeterminateSystems/nix-installer-action@3138316df39ed29be04236d7ffc686fa525866aa # v23

      - name: Allow unprivileged user namespaces (for bwrap)
        # Ubuntu 24.04 ships with kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1
        # which blocks bubblewrap's user-namespace setup ("bwrap: setting up uid
        # map: Permission denied"). Disabling the restriction is the standard CI
        # workaround — bwrap then works in unprivileged mode, which is what the
        # nix runtime's sandbox expects.
        if: matrix.gate == 'control-integration'
        run: sudo sysctl -w kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0

      - name: Install the pinned Redis agent
        if: matrix.gate == 'control-integration'
        run: codefly agent install codefly.dev/redis:0.0.74

      - name: Run the in-process run-profile proof
        if: matrix.gate == 'control-integration'
        run: go test -tags=integration -run '^TestRunProfilesStartRealDependencyShapesInProcess$' ./pkg/control -v

      # Pull separately from the proof below so a cold-cache image fetch is
      # attributed to its own step instead of inflating the test's wall time —
      # this gate shares one 8-minute job budget with the Nix install above.
      # Keep the tag in step with teardownPostgresImage in
      # pkg/orchestration/teardown_postgres_integration_test.go.
      - name: Pull the ordered-teardown proof's database image
        if: matrix.gate == 'control-integration'
        run: docker pull postgres:16-alpine

      # Ordered teardown (F09): the consumer holds its drain open and commits a
      # final transaction to a disposable Postgres; the database must not begin
      # stopping until that commit returned. Needs Docker, which the runner has.
      # It claims no conformance row: the ordering contract is backend-neutral,
      # so it proves nothing about a docs/supported-matrix.md row.
      - name: Run the ordered-teardown acceptance proof
        if: matrix.gate == 'control-integration'
        run: go test -tags=integration -run '^TestFlowStopHoldsPostgresUntilItsConsumerCommits$' ./pkg/orchestration -v

      # Always-run so a failed or filtered-out test still has to account for
      # the rows its job claimed. Keep these last: they audit every step above.
      - name: Verify conformance receipts
        if: always() && matrix.conformance_rows != ''
        run: ./scripts/verify-conformance-receipts.sh

      - name: Upload conformance receipts
        if: always() && matrix.conformance_rows != ''
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4
        with:
          name: conformance-receipts-${{ matrix.gate }}
          path: conformance-receipts/
          if-no-files-found: warn

  # golangci-lint runs as its own job, not a quality gate, for two reasons:
  # only-new-issues has a well-defined baseline only against a pull-request base
  # branch (on push there is no diff to gate against), and a cold-cache
  # whole-repository analysis needs more headroom than the 5-minute quality
  # budget. Pinned to match the version documented in the Makefile (`make
  # lint`). only-new-issues gates the PR on newly introduced findings so the
  # pre-existing backlog does not block work while the standard is enforced.
  lint:
    name: lint
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - name: checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@fbc6f3992d24b796d5a048ff273f7fcc4a7b6c09 # v5

      - name: Set up Go
        uses: actions/setup-go@924ae3a1cded613372ab5595356fb5720e22ba16 # v6
        with:
          go-version-file: go.mod
          cache: false

      - name: golangci-lint
        uses: golangci/golangci-lint-action@4afd733a84b1f43292c63897423277bb7f4313a9 # v8
        with:
          # v2.13.1 bundles staticcheck (honnef.co/go/tools) v0.8.0, the first
          # release that understands Go 1.27 stdlib source; v2.12.2's v0.7.0
          # panics in its IR builder analyzing 1.27 packages. Keep in sync with
          # GOLANGCI_LINT_VERSION in the Makefile.
          version: v2.13.1
          # Build the linter from source under the module's Go toolchain
          # (1.27) instead of downloading the prebuilt binary, which is built
          # with an older Go and refuses to lint a module targeting a newer
          # one ("the Go language version used to build golangci-lint is lower
          # than the targeted Go version"). Matches `make lint`.
          install-mode: goinstall
          only-new-issues: true

  # pkg/web/go-grpc/out is a committed, generated artifact: web/dashboard builds
  # into it and go:embed ships it inside the CLI binary (see the Makefile's
  # `dashboard` target, which is the only other place it is produced).
  #
  # Nothing else in CI runs npm, so without this job a dependency bump under
  # web/dashboard changes package.json and package-lock.json, leaves out/
  # untouched, and passes every Go gate — TestHandlerServesDashboard included,
  # because that test asserts against the committed bundle and so cannot notice
  # that the bundle no longer corresponds to the declared dependencies. The
  # binary would ship a dashboard built from the old dependency tree while the
  # lockfile claimed the new one, and the drift would surface at the next manual
  # `make dashboard`, several merges downstream of the bump that caused it.
  #
  # The build is byte-reproducible from the lockfile, so a clean tree is a fair
  # gate rather than a flaky one.
  dashboard:
    name: dashboard
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - name: checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@fbc6f3992d24b796d5a048ff273f7fcc4a7b6c09 # v5

      - name: Set up Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7
        with:
          # Pinned rather than left to the runner default: this job's whole
          # value is that a dirty out/ means the dependencies moved, so the
          # toolchain producing out/ must not drift underneath it.
          node-version: '24'
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: web/dashboard/package-lock.json

      # npm ci, not npm install: it fails closed on a package.json that has
      # drifted from the lockfile instead of silently resolving something else.
      - name: Rebuild the embedded dashboard
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cd web/dashboard
          npm ci
          npm run build

      # --intent-to-add so a newly emitted asset (an untracked file) is visible
      # to `git diff`; without it the check would only catch modifications and
      # deletions, and a build that added a chunk would pass while out/ was
      # missing it.
      - name: Fail if the committed bundle is stale
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          git add --intent-to-add -- pkg/web/go-grpc/out
          if ! git diff --exit-code -- pkg/web/go-grpc/out; then
            echo "::error::pkg/web/go-grpc/out does not match a build of web/dashboard. Run 'make dashboard' and commit the result."
            exit 1
          fi

name: Release

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - "v*.*.*"

concurrency:
  group: release-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write
  id-token: write
  attestations: write
  artifact-metadata: write

jobs:
  release:
    name: Qualify and publish
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45
    steps:
      - name: Check out the tagged source
        uses: actions/checkout@fbc6f3992d24b796d5a048ff273f7fcc4a7b6c09 # v5
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Set up Go
        uses: actions/setup-go@924ae3a1cded613372ab5595356fb5720e22ba16 # v6
        with:
          go-version-file: go.mod
          cache: false

      - name: Install Syft
        id: syft
        uses: anchore/sbom-action/download-syft@e22c389904149dbc22b58101806040fa8d37a610 # v0
        with:
          syft-version: v1.44.0

      - name: Load and verify the release signing key
        env:
          CODEFLY_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY_PATH: ${{ runner.temp }}/codefly-release-signing-key.pem
          RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY: ${{ secrets.CODEFLY_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          umask 077
          printf '%s' "$RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY" > "$CODEFLY_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY_PATH"
          openssl pkey -in "$CODEFLY_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY_PATH" -check -noout
          key_fingerprint="$(
            openssl pkey -in "$CODEFLY_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY_PATH" -pubout -outform DER |
              sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1
          )"
          certificate_fingerprint="$(
            openssl x509 -in pkg/cliupdate/release-signing-cert.pem -pubkey -noout |
              openssl pkey -pubin -outform DER |
              sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1

      - name: Qualify the clean tag
        env:
          CODEFLY_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY_PATH: ${{ runner.temp }}/codefly-release-signing-key.pem
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ github.ref_name }}
          SYFT_PATH: ${{ steps.syft.outputs.cmd }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          manifest_version="$(sed -n 's/^version:[[:space:]]*//p' pkg/cli/info.yaml)"
          test "$RELEASE_TAG" = "v$manifest_version"
          test "$(git rev-list -n 1 "$RELEASE_TAG")" = "$GITHUB_SHA"
          git diff --exit-code
          # The released Gateway imports Core's tree-sitter-backed project
          # inspection. Build inside the maintained cross image so the clean
          # tag is qualified with CGO and real compilers for every target.
          docker run --rm \
            -e CODEFLY_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY_PATH \
            -e RELEASE_TAG \
            -v "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE:/workspace" \
            -v "$RUNNER_TEMP:$RUNNER_TEMP" \
            -v "$SYFT_PATH:/usr/local/bin/syft:ro" \
            -w /workspace \
            ghcr.io/goreleaser/goreleaser-cross:v1.26.4 \
            check
          docker run --rm \
            -e CODEFLY_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY_PATH \
            -e RELEASE_TAG \
            -v "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE:/workspace" \
            -v "$RUNNER_TEMP:$RUNNER_TEMP" \
            -v "$SYFT_PATH:/usr/local/bin/syft:ro" \
            -w /workspace \
            ghcr.io/goreleaser/goreleaser-cross:v1.26.4 \
            release --snapshot --clean

          for target in darwin:amd64 darwin:arm64 linux:amd64 linux:arm64; do
            goos="${target%%:*}"
            goarch="${target##*:}"
            jq -e --arg goos "$goos" --arg goarch "$goarch" \
              '[.[] | select(.type == "Archive" and .goos == $goos and .goarch == $goarch)] | length == 1' \
              dist/artifacts.json
          done
          jq -e '[.[] | select(.type == "SBOM")] | length == 4' dist/artifacts.json
          jq -e '[.[] | select(.type == "Signature")] | length == 1' dist/artifacts.json
          test -s dist/checksums.txt
          test -s dist/checksums.txt.sig

          openssl x509 -in pkg/cliupdate/release-signing-cert.pem -pubkey -noout > "$RUNNER_TEMP/codefly-release-public-key.pem"
          openssl dgst -sha256 \
            -verify "$RUNNER_TEMP/codefly-release-public-key.pem" \
            -signature dist/checksums.txt.sig \
            dist/checksums.txt
          (cd dist && sha256sum --check checksums.txt)

      - name: Publish the immutable release and Homebrew cask
        env:
          CODEFLY_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY_PATH: ${{ runner.temp }}/codefly-release-signing-key.pem
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GH_PAT }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GH_PAT }}
          HOMEBREW_TAP_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GH_PAT }}
          MACOS_SIGN_P12: ${{ secrets.CODEFLY_MACOS_SIGN_P12 }}
          MACOS_SIGN_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.CODEFLY_MACOS_SIGN_PASSWORD }}
          MACOS_NOTARY_ISSUER_ID: ${{ secrets.CODEFLY_MACOS_NOTARY_ISSUER_ID }}
          MACOS_NOTARY_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.CODEFLY_MACOS_NOTARY_KEY_ID }}
          MACOS_NOTARY_KEY: ${{ secrets.CODEFLY_MACOS_NOTARY_KEY }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ github.ref_name }}
          SYFT_PATH: ${{ steps.syft.outputs.cmd }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          test "$(gh api "repos/codefly-dev/cli/commits/$RELEASE_TAG" --jq .sha)" = "$GITHUB_SHA"
          docker run --rm \
            -e CODEFLY_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY_PATH \
            -e GITHUB_TOKEN \
            -e GH_TOKEN \
            -e HOMEBREW_TAP_GITHUB_TOKEN \
            -e MACOS_SIGN_P12 \
            -e MACOS_SIGN_PASSWORD \
            -e MACOS_NOTARY_ISSUER_ID \
            -e MACOS_NOTARY_KEY_ID \
            -e MACOS_NOTARY_KEY \
            -e RELEASE_TAG \
            -v "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE:/workspace" \
            -v "$RUNNER_TEMP:$RUNNER_TEMP" \
            -v "$SYFT_PATH:/usr/local/bin/syft:ro" \
            -w /workspace \
            ghcr.io/goreleaser/goreleaser-cross:v1.26.4 \
            release --clean

  attest:
    name: Attest published artifacts
    needs: release
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write
      attestations: write
      artifact-metadata: write
    steps:
      - name: Download published artifacts
        env:
          # The repository-scoped workflow token is the read authority for this
          # job. GH_PAT is needed only by publication because it also updates the
          # separate Homebrew repository; carrying it into verification made a
          # successfully published release appear absent to `gh release`.
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-assets"
          gh release download "$RELEASE_TAG" \
            --repo codefly-dev/cli \
            --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-assets" \
            --pattern "codefly_*.tar.gz" \
            --pattern "codefly_*.sbom.json" \
            --pattern checksums.txt

      - name: Attest released archives
        uses: actions/attest@1e69f48acb82d1966a394da916b4c1698aa569d6 # v4
        with:
          subject-checksums: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-assets/checksums.txt

      - name: Attest published SBOMs
        uses: actions/attest@1e69f48acb82d1966a394da916b4c1698aa569d6 # v4
        with:
          subject-path: "${{ runner.temp }}/release-assets/*.sbom.json"

  verify:
    name: Verify published release
    needs: attest
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Check out the tagged source
        uses: actions/checkout@fbc6f3992d24b796d5a048ff273f7fcc4a7b6c09 # v5

      - name: Verify the published release
        env:
          # Verification reads this repository only and must not depend on the
          # cross-repository publication credential.
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          version="${RELEASE_TAG#v}"
          release_json="$(
            gh api \
              -H "X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2026-03-10" \
              "repos/codefly-dev/cli/releases/tags/$RELEASE_TAG"
          )"
          test "$(jq -r .immutable <<<"$release_json")" = "true"
          test "$(gh api "repos/codefly-dev/cli/commits/$RELEASE_TAG" --jq .sha)" = "$GITHUB_SHA"

          openssl x509 -in pkg/cliupdate/release-signing-cert.pem -pubkey -noout > "$RUNNER_TEMP/codefly-release-public-key.pem"

          for target in darwin_amd64 darwin_arm64 linux_amd64 linux_arm64; do
            archive="codefly_${version}_${target}.tar.gz"
            sbom="${archive}.sbom.json"
            jq -e --arg name "$archive" '[.assets[].name] | index($name) != null' <<<"$release_json"
            jq -e --arg name "$sbom" '[.assets[].name] | index($name) != null' <<<"$release_json"
          done
          for name in checksums.txt checksums.txt.sig; do
            jq -e --arg name "$name" '[.assets[].name] | index($name) != null' <<<"$release_json"
          done

          verify_dir="$(mktemp -d)"
          gh release download "$RELEASE_TAG" \
            --repo codefly-dev/cli \
            --dir "$verify_dir" \
            --pattern "codefly_${version}_*.tar.gz" \
            --pattern "codefly_${version}_*.sbom.json" \
            --pattern checksums.txt \
            --pattern checksums.txt.sig
          openssl dgst -sha256 \
            -verify "$RUNNER_TEMP/codefly-release-public-key.pem" \
            -signature "$verify_dir/checksums.txt.sig" \
            "$verify_dir/checksums.txt"
          (cd "$verify_dir" && sha256sum --check checksums.txt)
          for artifact in \
            "$verify_dir"/codefly_"${version}"_*.tar.gz \
            "$verify_dir"/codefly_"${version}"_*.sbom.json; do
            gh attestation verify "$artifact" --repo codefly-dev/cli
          done

          RELEASE_PRERELEASE="$(jq -r .prerelease <<<"$release_json")" \
            RELEASE_TAG="$RELEASE_TAG" \
            sh .github/scripts/verify-homebrew-cask.sh

      - run: bun run check
      - run: bun run build
      - run: bun dist/bunko.js version
      - run: bun run test:bundled-smoke
      - name: Prepare candidate
        id: candidate
        run: |
          bun run release:prepare
          bun -e 'import p from "./package.json"; import { appendFileSync } from "node:fs"; appendFileSync(process.env.GITHUB_OUTPUT!, "version=v" + p.version + "\n");'
      - uses: ./

          distribution-directory: dist/release
          bun-version: ${{ matrix.bun }}
      - run: bunko version
      - name: Prepare local Action base

      - uses: ./build
        id: action-build

  # sentinel into the managed cache before its build and must report a miss; the warm job must report an exact
  # hit on the identical key and find the sentinel, which proves cached bytes were restored, not just a key.
  action-cache-cold:
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest]

    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:

      - uses: ./
        with:
          version: ${{ steps.candidate.outputs.version }}
          distribution-directory: dist/release
          bun-version: 1.4.2
      - name: Prepare local Action base
        run: bun -e 'import {baseLayout} from "./test/helpers.ts"; await baseLayout(process.env.RUNNER_TEMP + "/action-base");'
      - name: Seed a sentinel into the managed cache

          mkdir -p "$HOME/.cache/bunko"

name: CLI container

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: Published CLI release to package
        required: true
        default: v0.7.0

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: cli-container-publication
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  publish:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write
      id-token: write
      attestations: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6 # v2.2.0
        with:
          bun-version: 1.4.2
      - name: Select an immutable published release
        id: release
        env:
          SELECTED_VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
        run: |
          test "$GITHUB_REF" = refs/heads/main
          bun -e 'import { releaseTag } from "./scripts/distribution.ts"; import {appendFileSync} from "node:fs"; const tag=releaseTag(process.env.SELECTED_VERSION!); appendFileSync(process.env.GITHUB_OUTPUT!, `tag=${tag}\nversion=${tag.slice(1)}\n`);'
      - name: Download and verify the CLI payload
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ steps.release.outputs.tag }}
        run: |
          mkdir -p dist/release
          gh release download "$RELEASE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --dir dist/release
          cd dist/release
          sha256sum --check SHA256SUMS
          if [ "$RELEASE_TAG" = v0.1.0-rc.3 ]; then
            echo 'c441e95a41bb063b5bc1716e33c3f27bfbe606e156a9c2e1e8baddaa23394464  SHA256SUMS' | sha256sum --check
            echo '09486aa233147f781fb2068335d6b02fc4e5359853f2445573a5dfa5f2deb3cd  bunko.js' | sha256sum --check
          else
            cd ../..
            bun scripts/verify-release.ts dist/release "$RELEASE_TAG"
          fi
      - uses: docker/setup-qemu-action@c7c53464625b32c7a7e944ae62b3e17d2b600130 # v3
      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@8d2750c68a42422c14e847fe6c8ac0403b4cbd6f # v3
      - uses: docker/login-action@c94ce9fb468520275223c153574b00df6fe4bcc9 # v3
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ github.token }}
      - name: Refuse replacement of a published version tag
        env:
          IMAGE_REFERENCE: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}:${{ steps.release.outputs.tag }}
        run: |
          bun -e 'import {parseReference} from "./packages/oci/source.ts"; import {RegistryClient} from "./packages/oci/registry.ts"; const r=parseReference(process.env.IMAGE_REFERENCE!); const response=await new RegistryClient(r.registry).request(`/v2/${r.repository}/manifests/${r.reference}`, {method:"HEAD"}, [`repository:${r.repository}:pull,push`], [404]); if(response.status !== 404) throw new Error("Container version tag already exists; refusing replacement");'
      - name: Build a digest-addressed candidate once
        id: image
        uses: docker/build-push-action@10e90e3645eae34f1e60eeb005ba3a3d33f178e8 # v6
        with:
          context: .
          file: container/Dockerfile
          platforms: linux/amd64,linux/arm64
          build-args: |
            BUNKO_VERSION=${{ steps.release.outputs.version }}
            BUNKO_REVISION=${{ github.sha }}
          outputs: type=image,name=ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }},push-by-digest=true,name-canonical=true,push=true
          provenance: mode=max
          sbom: true
      - name: Validate the candidate and its compiled application on both platforms
        env:
          BUNKO_CONTAINER_VERSION: ${{ steps.release.outputs.version }}
          BUNKO_CONTAINER_IMAGE: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}@${{ steps.image.outputs.digest }}
        run: |
          for arch in amd64 arm64; do
            docker pull --platform "linux/$arch" "$BUNKO_CONTAINER_IMAGE"
            BUNKO_SMOKE_PLATFORMS="linux/$arch" bun scripts/validation/container-smoke.ts
            # Classic Docker image stores cannot retain both platforms under one index digest.
            docker image rm "$BUNKO_CONTAINER_IMAGE"
          done
      - name: Attest the container index
        uses: actions/attest@1e69f48acb82d1966a394da916b4c1698aa569d6 # v4.2.2
        with:
          subject-name: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}
          subject-digest: ${{ steps.image.outputs.digest }}
          push-to-registry: true
      - name: Verify candidate provenance
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          IMAGE_DIGEST: ${{ steps.image.outputs.digest }}
        run: |
          gh attestation verify "oci://ghcr.io/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY@$IMAGE_DIGEST" \
            --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --signer-workflow "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/.github/workflows/container.yml" \
            --source-ref "$GITHUB_REF" --source-digest "$GITHUB_SHA" --deny-self-hosted-runners
      - name: Promote the verified index without rebuilding
        env:
          IMAGE_REPOSITORY: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}
          IMAGE_DIGEST: ${{ steps.image.outputs.digest }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ steps.release.outputs.tag }}
        run: bun scripts/promote-container.ts "$IMAGE_REPOSITORY" "$IMAGE_DIGEST" "$RELEASE_TAG"

name: npm distribution

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - scripts/npm-package.ts
      - scripts/validation/npm-smoke.ts
      - scripts/distribution.ts
      - scripts/verify-release.ts
      - test/npm-package.test.ts
      - .github/workflows/npm.yml
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: Existing attested GitHub release to package
        required: true
        default: v0.7.0
      publish:
        description: Publish the verified tarball using npm trusted publishing
        type: boolean
        default: false

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: npm-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || 'publication' }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  prepare:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.package.outputs.version }}
      tag: ${{ steps.package.outputs.tag }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6 # v2.2.0
        with:
          bun-version: 1.4.2
      - uses: actions/setup-node@249970729cb0ef3589644e2896645e5dc5ba9c38 # v6
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          package-manager-cache: false
      - name: Select a release from main history
        env:
          SELECTED_VERSION: ${{ inputs.version || 'v0.7.0' }}
        run: |
          bun -e 'import {releaseTag} from "./scripts/distribution.ts"; import {appendFileSync} from "node:fs"; appendFileSync(process.env.GITHUB_ENV!, "RELEASE_TAG="+releaseTag(process.env.SELECTED_VERSION!)+"\n");'
      - name: Verify the published release before executing it
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          source_commit=$(git rev-parse "$RELEASE_TAG^{commit}")
          git merge-base --is-ancestor "$source_commit" origin/main
          mkdir -p dist/release
          gh release download "$RELEASE_TAG" --repo sakajunquality/bunko --dir dist/release
          BUNKO_ATTESTATION_SOURCE_DIGEST="$source_commit" bun scripts/verify-release.ts dist/release "$RELEASE_TAG"
      - name: Package unchanged release bytes
        id: package
        run: |
          bun scripts/npm-package.ts dist/release dist/npm "$RELEASE_TAG"
          bun -e 'import {appendFileSync} from "node:fs"; const p=await Bun.file("dist/npm/package.json").json(); appendFileSync(process.env.GITHUB_OUTPUT!, "version="+p.version+"\ntag="+p.publishConfig.tag+"\n");'
      - name: Test the packed npm and bunx consumer
        run: bun scripts/validation/npm-smoke.ts dist/npm dist/npm-artifact
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: npm-candidate
          path: dist/npm-artifact/
          if-no-files-found: error

  publish:
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.publish && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    needs: prepare
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: npm
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/setup-node@249970729cb0ef3589644e2896645e5dc5ba9c38 # v6
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          package-manager-cache: false
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: npm-candidate
          path: candidate
      - name: Check the npm client and candidate integrity
        run: |
          node --input-type=module -e 'import {execFileSync} from "node:child_process"; const [major,minor,patch]=execFileSync("npm",["--version"],{encoding:"utf8"}).trim().split(".").map(Number); if(!(major>11 || major===11 && (minor>5 || minor===5 && patch>=1))) throw new Error("npm >=11.5.1 is required");'
          node --input-type=module -e 'import {readFileSync,readdirSync} from "node:fs"; import {createHash} from "node:crypto"; const p=JSON.parse(readFileSync("candidate/validation.json")); const files=readdirSync("candidate").filter(name=>name.endsWith(".tgz")); if(files.length!==1 || files[0]!==p.filename) throw new Error("Unexpected candidate tarball"); const digest="sha512-"+createHash("sha512").update(readFileSync("candidate/"+files[0])).digest("base64"); if(digest!==p.integrity) throw new Error("Candidate integrity mismatch");'
      - name: Publish the tested tarball with provenance
        env:
          NPM_DIST_TAG: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.tag }}
        run: |
          npm publish ./candidate/*.tgz --access public --tag "$NPM_DIST_TAG" --provenance --ignore-scripts

  verify-published:
    timeout-minutes: 15
    needs: [prepare, publish]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6 # v2.2.0
        with:
          bun-version: 1.4.2
      - uses: actions/setup-node@249970729cb0ef3589644e2896645e5dc5ba9c38 # v6
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          package-manager-cache: false
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: npm-candidate
          path: candidate
      - name: Download and compare the exact published tarball
        env:
          PACKAGE_VERSION: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.version }}
          NPM_CONFIG_FETCH_TIMEOUT: '15000'
          NPM_CONFIG_FETCH_RETRIES: '0'
        run: |
          mkdir downloaded
          for attempt in $(seq 1 21); do
            if npm pack "@sakajunquality/bunko@$PACKAGE_VERSION" --ignore-scripts --json --pack-destination downloaded > downloaded/pack.json; then break; fi
            if [ "$attempt" = 21 ]; then exit 1; fi
            sleep 15
          done
          node --input-type=module -e 'import {readFileSync} from "node:fs"; import {createHash} from "node:crypto"; const expected=JSON.parse(readFileSync("candidate/validation.json")); const result=JSON.parse(readFileSync("downloaded/pack.json"))[0]; const actual="sha512-"+createHash("sha512").update(readFileSync("downloaded/"+result.filename)).digest("base64"); if(actual!==expected.integrity) throw new Error("Published tarball differs from tested candidate");'
      - name: Execute the published package in a clean consumer
        env:
          PACKAGE_VERSION: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.version }}
        run: |
          mkdir consumer
          cd consumer
          npm install --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund ../downloaded/*.tgz
          test "$(./node_modules/.bin/bunko version)" = "$PACKAGE_VERSION"
          mkdir ../bunx-consumer
          cd ../bunx-consumer
          test "$(bun x "@sakajunquality/bunko@$PACKAGE_VERSION" version)" = "$PACKAGE_VERSION"

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  RUSTFLAGS: "-D warnings"

jobs:
  check:
    name: check (${{ matrix.os }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [macos-latest, ubuntu-latest]

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5

      # ADR-0001 puts the shell on Tauri, which links the system WebView. macOS
      # has it; Linux needs the GTK/WebKit development headers.
      #
      # `cmake` and `libclang-dev` are Phase 13's: `llama-cpp-sys-2` builds
      # llama.cpp through CMake and generates its bindings with bindgen, which
      # dlopens libclang. Neither is a runtime dependency of anything shipped.
      - name: Install Tauri's Linux dependencies
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
            libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev libgtk-3-dev libayatana-appindicator3-dev \
            librsvg2-dev libsoup-3.0-dev libjavascriptcoregtk-4.1-dev \
            cmake libclang-dev

      # Phase 13 links llama.cpp through CMake (task 13.17).
      #
      #   MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET      -> rustc and the linker
      #   CMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET   -> the CMake build of ggml
      #
      # `llama-cpp-sys-2` forwards CMAKE_* variables from the environment as -D
      # defines. Without the second, ggml compiles below 10.15 and fails on
      # `std::filesystem`. Both are also in the workspace `.cargo/config.toml`,
      # which covers a local build; this covers a runner whose environment the
      # config does not reach first. RUSTFLAGS is not the place for either:
      # rustc rejects clang's `-mmacosx-version-min`.
      - name: Set the macOS deployment target
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: |
          echo "MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=11.0" >> $GITHUB_ENV
          echo "CMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=11.0" >> $GITHUB_ENV

      - name: Install Rust
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: rustfmt, clippy

      # ADR-0003 builds SQLite from source, which dominates a cold build.
      - name: Cache cargo
        uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          shared-key: toolog

      # Phase 5.1 puts the window on TypeScript and Vite. The bundle is
      # embedded in the binary, so it is built before anything compiles it, and
      # `npm run build` type-checks first — a frontend that does not compile
      # must fail CI as loudly as a crate that does not.
      - name: Install Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: ui/package-lock.json

      - name: Build the window
        run: npm --prefix ui ci && npm --prefix ui run build

      - name: Frontend tests
        run: npm --prefix ui test

      - name: Format
        run: cargo fmt --all -- --check

      - name: Clippy
        run: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings

      - name: Test
        run: cargo test --workspace --all-targets

      # Task 13.19 reserved a build without inference as the fallback if the
      # universal build could not carry llama.cpp. It can — measured, and
      # recorded in the phase file — so the fallback is not taken. It is still
      # compiled here, because a fallback that does not build is not one, and
      # because it is what keeps the GGUF reader, the prompt and the verdict
      # schema free of the C++ they sit in front of.
      - name: The build without inference still builds
        run: cargo check -p toolog-llm --no-default-features --all-targets

      # The Rust/TypeScript boundary regenerates itself during the test run
      # (Phase 4.9). A diff here means someone changed a command or a type and
      # did not commit the bindings.
      - name: Generated bindings are committed
        run: git diff --exit-code -- ui/src/bindings.ts

  msrv:
    name: msrv
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - name: Install Tauri's Linux dependencies
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
            libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev libgtk-3-dev libayatana-appindicator3-dev \
            librsvg2-dev libsoup-3.0-dev libjavascriptcoregtk-4.1-dev \
            cmake libclang-dev
      - name: Install Rust (MSRV from Cargo.toml)
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@master
        with:
          toolchain: "1.95"
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          shared-key: msrv
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: ui/package-lock.json
      - run: npm --prefix ui ci && npm --prefix ui run build
      - run: cargo check --workspace --all-targets

name: Release

# Tag-driven (task 8.4). Pushing `v1.2.3` builds, signs, notarizes and
# publishes; nothing else does. The version in the artifacts comes from
# Cargo.toml, and the job refuses to run if the tag disagrees with it — a
# release named after a version the binary does not report is worse than no
# release.
on:
  push:
    tags: ["v*"]
  # Buildable without publishing, so the packaging can be exercised on a branch
  # without burning a version number.
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: write

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  # Pinned with the one in the justfile: a `.app` built here and a `.app` built
  # on a laptop must come from the same bundler.
  TAURI_CLI_VERSION: "2.11.4"

jobs:
  bundle:
    name: Universal bundle
    runs-on: macos-latest
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5

      - name: The tag and Cargo.toml agree
        id: version
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          version=$(awk '/^\[workspace\.package\]/{f=1} f && /^version = /{gsub(/[",]/,"",$3); print $3; exit}' Cargo.toml)
          echo "version=$version" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Cargo.toml says $version"
          if [ "${GITHUB_REF_TYPE:-}" = "tag" ]; then
            tag="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
            [ "$tag" = "$version" ] || {
              echo "::error::tag v$tag does not match Cargo.toml's $version"
              exit 1
            }
          fi

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: ui/package-lock.json

      # Phase 13 links llama.cpp through CMake (task 13.17).
      #
      #   MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET      -> rustc and the linker
      #   CMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET   -> the CMake build of ggml
      #
      # `llama-cpp-sys-2` forwards CMAKE_* variables from the environment as -D
      # defines. Without the second, ggml compiles below 10.15 and fails on
      # `std::filesystem`. Both are also in the workspace `.cargo/config.toml`,
      # which covers a local build; this covers a runner whose environment the
      # config does not reach first. RUSTFLAGS is not the place for either:
      # rustc rejects clang's `-mmacosx-version-min`.
      - name: Set the macOS deployment target
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: |
          echo "MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=11.0" >> $GITHUB_ENV
          echo "CMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=11.0" >> $GITHUB_ENV

      - name: Install Rust
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          targets: aarch64-apple-darwin,x86_64-apple-darwin

      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          shared-key: release

      - name: Install the pinned Tauri CLI
        run: cargo install tauri-cli --version "$TAURI_CLI_VERSION" --locked

      # The window is compiled into the binary, so it is built before anything
      # links it, and `npm run build` type-checks first.
      - name: Build the window
        run: npm --prefix ui ci && npm --prefix ui run build

      # ci.yml triggers on branches and pull requests, which a tag push does not
      # match — so without this a release could be cut from a tree whose tests
      # fail, and the artifact would be signed and notarized before anyone knew.
      # The bundle is built from this same checkout moments later.
      - name: Tests must pass before anything is signed
        run: |
          npm --prefix ui test
          cargo test --workspace --all-targets

      - name: Import the Developer ID certificate
        # Decoded into a throwaway keychain so `codesign` can reach the private
        # key, and deleted again in the cleanup step whatever happens.
        env:
          MACOS_CERT_P12_BASE64: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERT_P12_BASE64 }}
          MACOS_CERT_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERT_PASSWORD }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          KEYCHAIN=build.keychain-db
          KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD="$(openssl rand -hex 24)"
          CERT_PATH="${RUNNER_TEMP}/cert.p12"

          echo "$MACOS_CERT_P12_BASE64" | base64 --decode > "$CERT_PATH"

          security create-keychain -p "$KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD" "$KEYCHAIN"
          security set-keychain-settings -lut 21600 "$KEYCHAIN"
          security unlock-keychain -p "$KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD" "$KEYCHAIN"
          security import "$CERT_PATH" -k "$KEYCHAIN" -P "$MACOS_CERT_PASSWORD" \
            -T /usr/bin/codesign -T /usr/bin/security -T /usr/bin/xcrun
          security list-keychain -d user -s "$KEYCHAIN"
          security set-key-partition-list -S apple-tool:,apple: -s -k "$KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD" "$KEYCHAIN"

          echo "KEYCHAIN_PATH=$KEYCHAIN" >> $GITHUB_ENV
          echo "KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD=$KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD" >> $GITHUB_ENV
          echo "MACOS_CERT_PATH=$CERT_PATH" >> $GITHUB_ENV

      - name: Write the App Store Connect key
        env:
          APPLE_AUTH_KEY_P8_BASE64: ${{ secrets.APPLE_AUTH_KEY_P8_BASE64 }}
          APPLE_AUTH_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.APPLE_AUTH_KEY_ID }}
          APPLE_AUTH_KEY_ISSUER_ID: ${{ secrets.APPLE_AUTH_KEY_ISSUER_ID }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -z "$APPLE_AUTH_KEY_P8_BASE64" ] || [ -z "$APPLE_AUTH_KEY_ID" ] || [ -z "$APPLE_AUTH_KEY_ISSUER_ID" ]; then
            echo "::error::notarization needs APPLE_AUTH_KEY_P8_BASE64, APPLE_AUTH_KEY_ID and APPLE_AUTH_KEY_ISSUER_ID"
            exit 1
          fi
          KEY_DIR="${RUNNER_TEMP}/apple-auth-key"
          mkdir -p "$KEY_DIR"
          KEY_PATH="$KEY_DIR/AuthKey_${APPLE_AUTH_KEY_ID}.p8"
          echo "$APPLE_AUTH_KEY_P8_BASE64" | base64 --decode > "$KEY_PATH"
          chmod 600 "$KEY_PATH"
          # The names Tauri 2 reads for notarization.
          echo "APPLE_API_KEY_PATH=$KEY_PATH" >> $GITHUB_ENV
          echo "APPLE_API_KEY=$APPLE_AUTH_KEY_ID" >> $GITHUB_ENV
          echo "APPLE_API_ISSUER=$APPLE_AUTH_KEY_ISSUER_ID" >> $GITHUB_ENV

      - name: Bundle, signed
        env:
          APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY: ${{ secrets.APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY }}
          APPLE_API_KEY_PATH: ${{ env.APPLE_API_KEY_PATH }}
          APPLE_API_KEY: ${{ env.APPLE_API_KEY }}
          APPLE_API_ISSUER: ${{ env.APPLE_API_ISSUER }}
        run: cargo tauri build --target universal-apple-darwin

      - name: Notarize and staple the dmg
        # Tauri notarizes and staples the .app, but only *signs* the .dmg it
        # puts the app inside. A user downloads the .dmg, so the container has
        # to be notarized in its own right or the very first double-click is
        # the Gatekeeper warning this phase exists to avoid.
        env:
          APPLE_API_KEY_PATH: ${{ env.APPLE_API_KEY_PATH }}
          APPLE_API_KEY: ${{ env.APPLE_API_KEY }}
          APPLE_API_ISSUER: ${{ env.APPLE_API_ISSUER }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          shopt -s nullglob
          dmgs=(target/universal-apple-darwin/release/bundle/dmg/*.dmg)
          [ ${#dmgs[@]} -gt 0 ] || { echo "::error::no dmg was produced"; exit 1; }
          for dmg in "${dmgs[@]}"; do
            xcrun notarytool submit "$dmg" \
              --key "$APPLE_API_KEY_PATH" --key-id "$APPLE_API_KEY" \
              --issuer "$APPLE_API_ISSUER" --wait
            xcrun stapler staple "$dmg"
            xcrun stapler validate "$dmg"
          done

      - name: What a clean machine will see
        # The assertions that matter, run against the artifact rather than the
        # configuration. `spctl` here is the same question a first launch asks.
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          app=target/universal-apple-darwin/release/bundle/macos/toolog.app
          lipo -archs "$app/Contents/MacOS/toolog" | tee /dev/stderr | grep -q "x86_64" \
            || { echo "::error::not a universal binary"; exit 1; }
          codesign --verify --strict --deep --verbose=2 "$app"
          codesign -dv --verbose=4 "$app" 2>&1 | grep -q "flags=0x10000(runtime)" \
            || { echo "::error::the hardened runtime is not enabled"; exit 1; }
          # ADR-0008: the app asks for no entitlements. `[Dict]` with nothing
          # under it is what an empty entitlements dictionary prints as.
          ents=$(codesign -d --entitlements - "$app" 2>/dev/null | tail -n +2)
          [ "$(echo "$ents" | grep -c "<key>")" = "0" ] \
            || { echo "::error::the app is signed with entitlements: $ents"; exit 1; }
          spctl --assess --type execute --verbose=2 "$app"

      - name: Checksums
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cd target/universal-apple-darwin/release/bundle/dmg
          shasum -a 256 *.dmg > SHA256SUMS
          cat SHA256SUMS

      - name: Clean up the keychain
        if: always()
        run: |
          [ -n "${KEYCHAIN_PATH:-}" ] && security delete-keychain "$KEYCHAIN_PATH" || true
          security list-keychain -d user -s login.keychain-db
          rm -f "${MACOS_CERT_PATH:-}" "${APPLE_API_KEY_PATH:-}" || true

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: toolog-macos-universal
          path: |
            target/universal-apple-darwin/release/bundle/dmg/*.dmg
            target/universal-apple-darwin/release/bundle/dmg/SHA256SUMS
          if-no-files-found: error

  publish:
    name: Publish the release
    needs: bundle
    if: github.ref_type == 'tag'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: toolog-macos-universal
          path: dist

      - uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v2
        with:
          files: |
            dist/*.dmg
            dist/SHA256SUMS
          fail_on_unmatched_files: true
          generate_release_notes: true
          body: |
            ## Install

            ```
            brew install --cask zaghaghi/tap/toolog
            ```

            Or download the `.dmg` below. It is signed with a Developer ID and
            notarized by Apple, so it opens without a Gatekeeper warning.

            ## Verify what you downloaded

            ```
            shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS
            spctl --assess --type execute --verbose=2 /Applications/toolog.app
            ```

            ## What it does on your machine

            The receiver binds `127.0.0.1` only. There is no analytics, no crash
            reporting, no update check and no account — see
            [PRIVACY.md](https://github.com/zaghaghi/toolog/blob/main/PRIVACY.md).
            Removing it is one command: `toolog uninstall`, which puts
            `~/.claude/settings.json` back byte for byte and keeps your recorded
            history unless you ask for it to go.

[workspace]
resolver = "3"
members = ["crates/*"]

[workspace.package]
version = "1.2.0"
edition = "2024"
rust-version = "1.95"
license = "MIT"
authors = ["Hamed Zaghaghi <hamed.zaghaghi@gmail.com>"]
repository = "https://github.com/zaghaghi/toolog"
homepage = "https://github.com/zaghaghi/toolog"
description = "A local audit trail for Claude Code tool calls"

# Versions pinned from crates.io at planning time. Members opt in individually
# with `dep.workspace = true`; declaring one here does not pull it into a build.
[workspace.dependencies]
# --- internal ---
toolog-core = { path = "crates/toolog-core" }
toolog-ingest = { path = "crates/toolog-ingest" }
toolog-otlp = { path = "crates/toolog-otlp" }
toolog-cli = { path = "crates/toolog-cli" }
toolog-llm = { path = "crates/toolog-llm" }

# --- storage (ADR-0003) ---
# `bundled` compiles SQLite from source: no system dependency, no version skew.
rusqlite = { version = "0.40.2", features = ["bundled", "hooks"] }
# No refinery: refinery-core 0.9.2 caps at rusqlite <=0.39, so it would force a
# downgrade or a second linked SQLite. Migrations are a hand-rolled
# `PRAGMA user_version` stepper instead — see toolog-core/src/migrations.rs.

# --- OTLP receiver (ADR-0005) ---
axum = "0.8.9"
tokio = { version = "1.53.1", features = ["rt-multi-thread", "macros", "sync", "fs", "signal"] }
# `gen-tonic-messages` gives the prost message types without the gRPC stack;
# `with-serde` makes the same types decode OTLP/JSON, so one crate serves both
# wire formats (verified against the JS exporter's int64-as-string encoding).
opentelemetry-proto = { version = "0.32.0", default-features = false, features = [
    "gen-tonic-messages",
    "logs",
    "with-serde",
] }
prost = "0.14.4"

# --- ingestion (ADR-0002) ---
notify = "8.2.0"
walkdir = "2.5.0"

# --- secret redaction (Phase 7.2) ---
# Already in the graph via `tauri-utils`, so this adds a direct dependency and
# no new compilation. Patterns are data a user can extend, which means they are
# compiled at runtime and must be able to fail without taking the process down.
regex = "1.13.1"

# --- risk rules as data (Phase 6.1) ---
# TOML rather than JSON, because this is a file users are meant to edit: literal
# strings need no backslash escaping, and comments survive.
toml = "0.9.8"

# --- serialization ---
serde = { version = "1.0.229", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = { version = "1.0.151", features = ["preserve_order"] }

# --- errors, logging, time, paths ---
anyhow = "1.0.104"
thiserror = "2.0.20"
tracing = "0.1.44"
tracing-subscriber = { version = "0.3.23", features = ["env-filter"] }
# Rotating local log files (Phase 4.11). Local disk only — never a network sink.
tracing-appender = "0.2.5"
jiff = "0.2.35"
directories = "6.0.0"

# --- hashing: raw_event dedup and the Phase 7 integrity chain (ADR-0004) ---
sha2 = "0.11.0"
hex = "0.4.3"

# --- the local second opinion (Phase 13, ADR-0013) ---
# `default-features = false` drops `openmp`, which Apple's clang does not ship,
# and `android-shared-stdcxx`, which is not this platform. `common` is not
# optional: `LlamaSampler::grammar` is behind it, and the GBNF grammar is what
# stops the model emitting anything but the schema (task 13.10). `metal` is
# added per-target by toolog-llm, because it is a macOS framework.
#
# This is the one dependency in the workspace that builds C++. It does **not**
# bring a network stack: llama-cpp-sys-2 passes `-DLLAMA_CURL=OFF` to CMake, and
# because a C library is invisible to the egress test's manifest check, that is
# asserted against the built binary instead — `just verify-bundle` (task 13.4).
llama-cpp-2 = { version = "0.1.150", default-features = false, features = [
    "common",
    "sampler",
] }

# --- test-only ---
tempfile = "3.27.0"

# --- CLI ---
clap = { version = "4.6.6", features = ["derive"] }

# --- desktop shell (ADR-0001) ---
tauri = { version = "2.11.5", features = ["tray-icon", "image-png"] }
tauri-build = "2.6.3"
tauri-plugin-single-instance = "2.4.4"
tauri-plugin-notification = "2.4.0"
tauri-plugin-opener = "2.5.5"
# The one dialog the app opens: "save this export where?". No network, and the
# path it returns is the only place the process writes outside its own store.
tauri-plugin-dialog = "2.4.1"

# --- the Rust/TypeScript boundary (Phase 4.9) ---
# A plain dependency rather than a feature: every type that crosses the IPC
# boundary lives in these crates, and a feature flag would let a build exist in
# which the bindings cannot be generated at all.
ts-rs = "12.0.1"

[workspace.lints.rust]
unsafe_code = "forbid"
missing_debug_implementations = "warn"
unreachable_pub = "warn"

[workspace.lints.clippy]
all = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }
pedantic = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }
# Noisy for a workspace whose crates are named after their domain.
module_name_repetitions = "allow"
# Docs are in ADRs and phase files; per-fn error sections are not the house style.
missing_errors_doc = "allow"
missing_panics_doc = "allow"
# Fires on any CamelCase word. These doc comments are architectural prose full of
# proper nouns (LaunchAgent, OpenTelemetry, SQLCipher); backticking them all would
# read worse than the lint is worth.
doc_markdown = "allow"

[profile.release]
lto = "thin"
codegen-units = 1
strip = true

    name: Test and Lint
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    container:
      image: fedora:latest

    steps:
      - name: Install system dependencies
        run: |
          dnf install -y \
            git \
            gcc \
            pkgconf-pkg-config \
            gtk4-devel \
            libadwaita-devel \
            meson \
            ninja-build \
            gettext \
            desktop-file-utils \
            appstream \
            rust \
            cargo \
            clippy \
            rustfmt

      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Check code formatting
        run: cargo fmt --check

      - name: Run clippy
        run: cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings

      - name: Run tests
        run: cargo test --all-targets --all-features

      - name: Build and test with Meson
        run: |
          meson setup build
          ninja -C build test

[package]
name = "dropzone"
version = "1.1.0"
edition = "2024"
authors = ["dragonGR <alex@debtman.dev>"]
license = "GPL-3.0-or-later"
description = "Temporary file sharing over the local network"
homepage = "https://github.com/dragonGR/dropzone"
repository = "https://github.com/dragonGR/dropzone"
readme = "README.md"
keywords = ["gnome", "gtk4", "libadwaita", "file-sharing", "lan"]
categories = ["network-programming"]

[dependencies]
gtk4 = { version = "0.11", features = ["v4_16"] }
libadwaita = { version = "0.9", features = ["v1_6"] }
tokio = { version = "1.40", features = ["rt-multi-thread", "macros", "net", "io-util", "fs", "sync"] }
axum = { version = "0.8", default-features = false, features = ["http1", "tokio"] }
tokio-util = { version = "0.7", default-features = false, features = ["io"] }
qrcode = { version = "0.14.1", default-features = false }
if-addrs = "0.15"
rand = "0.8"
gettext-rs = { version = "0.8", features = ["gettext-system"] }

[profile.release]
opt-level = 3
lto = true
codegen-units = 1
panic = "abort"
strip = true
